text:
sophia: quick summary — ran a "staggered phase-packing" probe to reduce blocking all-reduces by pipelining cross-GPU comms across layers on 8xA100.
rahul: curious — how is "phase-packing" different from channel packing we've tried?
sophia: it's related but layer-aware: instead of packing tensors from the same layer onto multiple channels, we stagger which layers start their all-reduce windows so compute on later layers overlaps all-reduce for earlier ones. intent is to increase comm/compute overlap without increasing peak bandwidth.
kevin: numbers?
sophia: baseline (no stagger, 4 channels, NCCL_PROTO=LL128): throughput ~1120 tok/s, p99 latency 210ms. staggered (window shift=3 layers, 4 channels, LL128): throughput ~1290 tok/s (+15%), p99 160ms (-24%). small-batch (B=1,S=32) tail regressed ~6% though.
marta: interesting. what NCCL knobs did you flip?
sophia: envs set:
```
NCCL_ALGO=RING
NCCL_PROTO=LL128
NCCL_LL_THRESHOLD=4096
NCCL_MAX_NUMCHANNELS=4
``` 
and runtime changes: phase_shift_layers=3, channel_assignment=round_robin_by_tensor_size, kernel_selector prefers int8/quant path for FFN when seq_len>256.
jon: any artifacts in nsys?
sophia: pasted a trimmed nsys flame excerpt — see block. compute stripes show ~30-40% overlap with ncclAllReduce when staggered; baseline had <10% overlap.
```
# nsys flame snippet (timeline rows compressed)
compute_layer_12 |==========            
ncclAllReduce_l12  -----======          
compute_layer_11   ========            
ncclAllReduce_l11   ----======         
# overlap band increased in staggered run
``` 
rahul: did you try LL (non-128) vs LL128 tradeoff?
sophia: yes. LL128 wins for large messages (FFN shard > 64KB) with throughput wins. LL is better for micro-bursts and reduces per-op latency for very small tensors. we added a dynamic proto switch heuristic in the scheduler: if estimated allreduce_size < 8KB -> NCCL_PROTO=LL else LL128. that recovered small-batch latency.
kevin: how does KV cache warmup interact? I saw warmup spikes earlier.
sophia: good call — KV-cache prefetch generated extra small all-reduces early in the request which interfered with stagger windows. fix: tag KV-cache prefetch comms with low-prio channel and avoid scheduling them into the staggered packing frontier. reduced p99 warmup spikes by ~18%.
marta: any perf regressions on hetero machines (mixed mem/bandwidth)?
sophia: tested mixed 8xA100 + 1xA10 in ded clusters — stagger relies on predictable compute ordering; hetero slows a channel and causes backlog. mitigation: adaptive window shrinker — if measured compute lag > 10ms, reduce shift to 1 layer and fall back to single-channel packing.
jon: what's the runtime complexity of scheduler change?
sophia: O(num_layers + num_channels) per forward, tiny compared to kernel time. added deterministic assignment so traces are reproducible.
rahul: CI/test harness results?
ci-bot: staging rollout started for config: staggered_phase_packing=on, window_shift=3, dynamic_proto=on. smoke tests: 116/120 passed. failing cases are reproducible on B=1 tests (investigating). :eyes:
kevin: logs for failing smoke tests?
sophia: failures are small-batch latency asserts; root cause: our kernel selector sometimes chose quant kernels expecting larger batch when dynamic proto flipped. quick patch: add batch-aware kernel revalidation step before launch.
ops-bot: note — rolling change will have canary on 10% of dedicated clusters this afternoon.
marta: next steps: 1) land kernel revalidation patch 2) add explicit KV prefetch channel assignment 3) add hetero fallback tuning + experiment for window shrinker 4) extend perf dashboard with layerwise overlap metric.
jon: agree. also add a synthetic microbenchmark that reproduces B=1 path for QA.
rahul: thanks, super helpful. can you upload nsys traces + config to /mnt/bench/staggered_phasepacking/2005551234/ ?
sophia: uploaded: /mnt/bench/staggered_phasepacking/2005551234/{nsys_trace.zip,envs.txt,profile_summary.txt}. i'll open a PR with the scheduler patch and testcases.
